claims.statement: Backend recording start is strictly ordered: it first acquires the shared engine lifecycle lock, then rejects a second start via the IS_RECORDING atomic, then validates the transcription model (via validate_transcription_model_ready, which resolves the transcript config — defaulting to parakeet when missing — and initializes/validates the matching engine) before any stream is opened. On validation failure it emits a transcription-error event with actionable: false and aborts without opening streams.

Device resolution at start is Preference → Default → Error for the microphone (start fails if both preferred and default input are unavailable) and Preference → Default → None for system audio (recording continues mic-only with a warning). On macOS, default-device selection additionally overrides Bluetooth capture devices to built-in wired devices for stable sample rates.

A started session is kept alive by process-global statics: the RecordingManager is stored in RECORDING_MANAGER, IS_RECORDING is set true, and the transcription task's JoinHandle is stored in TRANSCRIPTION_TASK. A meeting name (provided or generated `Meeting <timestamp>`) is always set so the incremental saver initializes. After start, the backend emits recording-started and refreshes the tray menu.

At start the backend registers a transcript-update listener that converts each event payload into a TranscriptSegment and stores its Tauri EventId in TRANSCRIPT_LISTENER_ID; during stop that listener is explicitly unlistened so lingering references cannot keep the microphone active.

The ENGINE_LIFECYCLE_LOCK serializes recording start/stop against batch jobs: acquire_engine_lifecycle_lock is taken by recording start, and unload_engine_after_batch takes the same lock and skips model unloading while a live recording is active.

RecordingSaver.start_accumulation initializes the meeting folder and IncrementalAudioSaver only when the user's auto_save preference is on; otherwise it creates the folder for transcripts/metadata but skips .checkpoints/ and discards audio chunks. The folder is created as <recordings>/<sanitized name>_<YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM>/ with a .checkpoints/ subdirectory when checkpoints are enabled.

IncrementalAudioSaver buffers pre-mixed audio and, whenever the buffer reaches 30 seconds (sample_rate × 30 = 1,440,000 samples at 48 kHz), encodes it as a mono checkpoint file .checkpoints/audio_chunk_NNN.mp4; finalize() writes any final partial checkpoint, errors with 'No audio checkpoints' when zero checkpoints exist, and is the source of crash-survivable audio.

Transcripts are persisted continuously during recording: each transcript-update event is upserted into RecordingSaver's segment list keyed by sequence_id, and every add rewrites transcripts.json to the meeting folder using an atomic temp-file-then-rename write (as does metadata.json).

The transcription task runs a single serial worker (NUM_WORKERS = 1) so transcripts emit in chronological order, and for each accepted chunk assigns a monotonic sequence_id, derives recording-relative audio_start_time/audio_end_time/duration from the chunk timestamp, emits speech-detected exactly once per session (session-scoped flag reset at start), and emits the transcript-update event.

The transcription task enforces zero chunk loss via chunks_queued/chunks_completed counters: workers poll until input is finished and all queued chunks are completed, the dispatcher's final verification waits (10 attempts) for the counters to agree, and a residual mismatch emits the transcript-chunk-loss-detected event.

Transcription failure semantics: engine initialization failure at task start emits an actionable transcription-error and ends the task; per chunk, a model unloaded mid-session causes skip-but-count (chunk preserved in accounting), AudioTooShort and ModelNotLoaded are skipped silently as expected, and other provider failures emit transcription-warning (with transcription-error payloads from the provider adapters).

Pause/resume are guarded state transitions on RecordingState (pause fails when not recording or already paused, resume when not paused); while paused, audio chunks are silently discarded (send_audio_chunk returns Ok without sending) so paused time contributes no audio, and each transition emits recording-paused/recording-resumed and refreshes the tray menu; is_recording_paused exposes the state for polling.

RecordingStateContext is the single source of truth for the frontend lifecycle status (RecordingStatus: IDLE/STARTING/RECORDING/STOPPING/PROCESSING_TRANSCRIPTS/SAVING/COMPLETED/ERROR). It syncs with the backend via listeners on recording-started/stopped/paused/resumed, an initial mount sync via get_recording_state that fixes the refresh-desync bug, and 500 ms polling of get_recording_state while recording.

get_recording_state returns is_recording, is_paused, is_active, recording_duration, active_duration, total_pause_duration, and current_pause_duration — with null/0 fallbacks when no manager exists — and the RecordingStateContext poller maps these into React state.

Two complementary mechanisms recover UI state after a webview reload during an active recording: useRecordingStateSync polls is_recording every 1 s and re-adopts (or drops) the session in local state, and TranscriptContext pulls the full segment history from get_transcript_history plus the meeting name from get_recording_meeting_name when it finds itself recording with an empty local transcript list.

AudioDeviceMonitor polls the device list every 2 s while recording (5 s when all devices are present), classifies devices as Bluetooth by name heuristic (e.g. AirPods/Bluetooth/Wireless), declares a disconnect only after 2 consecutive missing checks for wired devices or 3 for Bluetooth, emits DeviceReconnected when a missing device reappears, and queues events on an unbounded channel.

Device reconnection is exposed to the frontend through three registered commands: poll_audio_device_events (drains one queued DeviceEvent; designed for 1–2 s polling during recording), get_reconnection_status (whether a reconnect is in progress and which device is marked disconnected), and attempt_device_reconnect (the UI Retry: re-enumerates devices and restarts streams with the other device preserved, requiring an active recording).

The Bluetooth playback warning surface: get_active_audio_output reports the default output device with a per-platform Bluetooth name heuristic, and BluetoothPlaybackWarning polls it every 5 s to render a dismissible alert when the active output is Bluetooth, resetting the dismissal when the user switches back to a non-Bluetooth output. This addresses playback distortion of 48 kHz recordings over Bluetooth (documented in BLUETOOTH_PLAYBACK_NOTICE.md), not a recording defect.

The backend stop first takes the manager out of RECORDING_MANAGER and calls stop_streams_and_force_flush, which stops the device monitor first (avoiding slow Windows WASAPI polling), stops streams, sends empty-chunk flush signals so the pipeline drains accumulated audio immediately, and fully clears device references via RecordingState cleanup so the microphone is released even if Drop is delayed; each stage emits recording-shutdown-progress.

Stop ordering guarantees zero transcript chunk loss before teardown: the stored transcription task handle is awaited (with a 500 ms progress reporter and a hard 10-minute cap to prevent indefinite hangs) and only then is the transcription model unloaded — Parakeet when the configured provider is parakeet, Whisper otherwise (config fetch itself capped at 30 s).

During stop the backend tracks meeting-ended analytics with privacy-safe metadata — device types classified from device names (Bluetooth vs Wired), provider/model names, total/active/pause durations, chunk and segment counts, and fatal-error flag — and analytics failures are logged without blocking shutdown.

Stop persists recording artifacts via manager.save_recording_only (capped at 5 minutes, failures non-fatal), which runs RecordingSaver.stop_and_save: IncrementalAudioSaver.finalize() merges all checkpoints into <folder>/audio.mp4 with FFmpeg concat (-c copy, no re-encode) and deletes .checkpoints/, the final transcripts.json is written and verified, and metadata.json is updated to status completed with the actual recording duration.

After teardown the backend clears IS_RECORDING and emits recording-stopped with { folder_path, meeting_name } for the frontend — it deliberately performs no database save, deferring the SQLite save until after all transcripts have streamed into the UI.

useRecordingStop listens for recording-stopped, stores folder_path and meeting_name in sessionStorage (last_recording_folder_path / last_recording_meeting_name), and records the handler as a promise so the stop flow awaits that data before proceeding, closing the race with the backend's stop completion.

The frontend stop flow waits for transcription completion by polling get_transcription_status every 500 ms up to 60 s (also listening for transcription-complete; done when not processing with an empty queue or after 8 s inactivity with an empty queue), then waits 4 s for late segments, force-flushes the transcript buffer via TranscriptContext.flushBuffer() (processing all remaining buffered entries regardless of timing), and waits 500 ms for state updates before saving.

The wait-for-completion poll relies on get_transcription_status, which is registered as a stub that always reports an idle queue (chunks_in_queue 0, is_processing false, last_activity 0), and nothing in the active backend emits transcription-complete — so the frontend wait returns on the first poll and the real draining guarantee is the backend's awaited transcription task during stop.

The SQLite save uses the backend-provided meeting name (savedMeetingName preferred over the locally generated title) and the folder_path from sessionStorage, calling storageService.saveMeeting → api_save_transcript (which persists via TranscriptsRepository::save_transcript and returns meeting_id); it also applies the pinned summary-language preference to the new meeting or, failing that, detects the summary language, with non-fatal warnings.

After a successful save the frontend marks the meeting saved in IndexedDB (markMeetingAsSaved, also clearing sessionStorage.indexeddb_current_meeting_id), removes the recording sessionStorage keys, refetches the sidebar meeting list, sets the current meeting, shows a success toast with a View Meeting action, tracks meeting-completed analytics (duration from transcript timestamps, word count, WPM, first-meeting activation), and after 2 s auto-navigates to /meeting-details?id={meetingId}&source=recording, resetting status to IDLE; analytics errors never block the flow.

Tray-initiated stop calls audio::recording_commands::stop_recording directly in Rust and then emits recording-stop-complete, which RecordingPostProcessingProvider handles app-wide by invoking handleRecordingStop — so post-stop processing works from any page. handleRecordingStop guards against duplicate/concurrent stops (stopInProgressRef) and is also exposed as window.handleRecordingStop for Rust-initiated callbacks.

Auto-summary is armed on the meeting-details page only when navigated with source=recording and the user's auto-summary toggle is enabled; with a configured model in the database (or gemma3:1b as fallback when the DB is empty) the page sets shouldAutoGenerate, and PageContent kicks off summary generation once transcripts are loaded.

TranscriptContext journals the live meeting for crash recovery: on recording-started it generates a meeting-{timestamp} IndexedDB id (mirrored to sessionStorage.indexeddb_current_meeting_id), initializes meeting metadata with the backend meeting name and folder path (get_meeting_folder_path), and while a meeting id is active writes every transcript update to IndexedDB non-blocking (failures swallowed so recording is never interrupted).

The home page runs startup recovery checks (skipped while recording or mid-stop-flow): it prunes IndexedDB meetings older than 7 days and saved meetings older than 24 h, then checks for recoverable meetings; if any exist it shows the TranscriptRecovery dialog once per session (guarded by a sessionStorage flag).

useTranscriptRecovery.checkForRecoverableTranscripts lists unsaved IndexedDB meetings within a 7-day retention window (excluding the last 2 seconds so the just-finished session is not caught) and verifies audio availability per meeting via has_audio_checkpoints, clearing folderPath when no checkpoint audio exists so the UI shows 'No audio'.

recoverMeeting loads IndexedDB metadata and transcripts, resolves the folder path (falling back to the backend's get_meeting_folder_path), invokes recover_audio_from_checkpoints, saves the meeting through storageService.saveMeeting, marks it saved in IndexedDB, cleans up checkpoint files (non-fatal on failure), and removes it from the recoverable list; the home page toasts the result and auto-navigates to the recovered meeting.

Three Tauri commands support checkpoint recovery: has_audio_checkpoints reports whether a folder's .checkpoints/ contains .mp4 files; recover_audio_from_checkpoints sorts the checkpoints, merges them into <folder>/audio.mp4 with FFmpeg concat, and returns status success/failed/none with chunk count and estimated duration (~30 s per chunk); cleanup_checkpoints removes the directory after a successful save or recovery.

useRecordingStart gates every start entry point (manual button, auto-start from sessionStorage.autoStartRecording after sidebar navigation, and the start-recording-from-sidebar window event) behind a Parakeet readiness check (parakeet_init + parakeet_has_available_models, distinguishing a Downloading state with a wait toast from a missing-model error with the model-selector modal) before invoking the backend; on success it sets the generated title (Meeting DD_MM_YY_HH_MM_SS), status STARTING, and calls startRecordingWithDevices; failures set status ERROR and reset local state.

The UI stop generates a save_path (<appDataDir>/recording-<timestamp>.wav) and invokes the stop_recording command with it, then triggers the frontend post-processing via onRecordingStop(true); device-specific start failures (microphone/system audio/permission) are classified in RecordingControls to show targeted error hints.
